rationale: Both candidates independently zero in on the sole ground-truth concern (the already_submitted gating removal), reasoning through the same submit_initial/submit_update code paths the human reviewer flagged, so recall is comparable. X is organized around a clear verdict and prioritized fix list with concrete file:line citations (including plausible edge cases like len>1 crashes and the else-branch bypass), but its headline 'blocker' claim that super().forward() is signature-broken by an unrelated prior refactor is a large, dramatic, unverified assertion not corroborated by Y's independent deep validation of the same code paths, creating real precision risk. Y is safer and grounds nearly every claim in quoted code/line evidence including a runnable test suggestion, but pads its report with many near-duplicate 'resolved' bullets restating the same 1-2 findings, diluting actionability without adding real coverage.
